1.title: Transform and Process Data
1.text: Welcome to Module three: Transform and Process Data. This module covers the task statement: transform and process data. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. Choose the transformation service that fits a requirement: A W S Glue, Amazon E M R (Elastic MapReduce), A W S Lambda, Amazon Redshift, Athena. Convert formats (for example C S V to Apache Parquet) and know why. Connect to data sources with J D B C (Java Database Connectivity) and O D B C (Open Database Connectivity) and integrate several sources. Optimize cost and container usage while processing. Troubleshoot common transformation failures and slow jobs. Publish data through A P I s and describe volume, velocity and variety.

1.title: Case Check-In: Kestrel Freight Cleans Its Data
1.text: Our running case is Kestrel Freight. Kestrel Freight Cleans Its Data. Nightly order C S V files have mixed date formats and duplicates. Truck telemetry needs a join with the vehicle register held in a database. Analysts want Parquet files that Athena can scan cheaply. A delivery notes field holds free text that someone must classify. Your job: pick the right engine for each step.

1.title: Choosing the Transformation Service
1.text: Choosing the Transformation Service. The figure shows this: Choosing a transformation service: A W S Glue for serverless E T L (extract, transform, load), Amazon E M R for control and scale, Lambda for small event-driven steps, Redshift or Athena for S Q L, and DataBrew for visual preparation.

1.title: Choosing the Transformation Service, continued
1.text: Choosing the Transformation Service, continued. A W S Glue. Best for: Serverless Apache Spark E T L (and Python shell) with the Data Catalog, crawlers, bookmarks, workflows. Remember: Pay for D P U s (data processing unit) while jobs run; no clusters to manage; Flex execution for non-urgent jobs. Amazon E M R. Best for: Big data frameworks (Spark, Hive, Presto, Flink, HBase) with full control of versions, libraries and tuning. Remember: E M R on E C two (Elastic Compute Cloud) (clusters), E M R on E K S (Elastic Kubernetes Service), E M R Serverless; Spot instances cut cost; transient clusters for batch. A W S Lambda. Best for: Small, event-driven transformations (one file, one record batch). Remember: fifteen-minute limit, memory-bound; great for glue code and light E T L.

1.title: Choosing the Transformation Service, continued
1.text: Choosing the Transformation Service, continued. Amazon Redshift. Best for: S Q L transformations inside the warehouse (E L T): insert... select, materialized views, stored procedures. Remember: Data is loaded first, transformed in place. Amazon Athena. Best for: S Q L E T L on S three with create table as select (C T A S) and insert into. Remember: Serverless, pay per data scanned. A W S Glue DataBrew. Best for: Visual, no-code cleaning and preparation (two hundred fifty plus transforms). Remember: For analysts, with profiling and recipes. Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink. Best for: Stateful stream processing. Remember: Module two.

1.title: Glue facts to know
1.text: Glue facts to know. A D P U (data processing unit) is four virtual C P Us and sixteen gigabytes of memory; worker types include G one X (one D P U), G two X (two), G four X (four), G eight X (eight) and memory-optimized R types; G point zero two five X is only for low-volume streaming jobs. Job types: Spark (batch), Spark Streaming, Python shell (small jobs, no Spark). Retries: zero to ten automatic restarts; timeouts are not retried. Maximum concurrency defaults to one run of the same job.

1.title: Glue facts to know, continued
1.text: Glue facts to know, continued. Flex execution (jobs on Glue three point zero or later with G one X or G two X workers) is cheaper and for non-urgent work (testing, one-time loads); standard execution is for time-sensitive work. Job run queuing lets runs wait instead of failing when quotas are hit. Glue Data Catalog as Hive metastore lets Spark, E M R and Athena share table definitions.

1.title: EMR facts to know
1.text: E M R facts to know. Amazon E M R (formerly Elastic MapReduce) is a managed cluster platform for Hadoop, Spark and related tools. Node types: primary (coordinates), core (H D F S storage and tasks), task (compute only, ideal for Spot). E M R Serverless: pick a runtime (Spark or Hive), submit jobs, and it scales workers automatically and releases them; pre-initialized capacity keeps workers warm for fast starts. Use S three (E M R F S) for durable data and transient clusters that stop when the job ends. Exam tip: "Serverless, minimal operations, E T L with a catalog" to Glue. "Need a specific Spark or Hive version, custom libraries or Hadoop ecosystem tools" to E M R. "Occasional small transformation when a file arrives" to Lambda.

1.title: File Formats and Conversion
1.text: File Formats and Conversion. The figure shows this: Row storage keeps whole records together; columnar storage keeps each column together, so analytic queries read less data and cost less.

1.title: File Formats and Conversion, continued
1.text: File Formats and Conversion, continued. C S V, T S V (tab-separated values). Layout: Row, text. Use it for: Exchange and simple loads; no schema, no types; large files are split only if uncompressed. Jason. Layout: Row, text, semi-structured. Use it for: A P I s and logs; nested data; verbose. Avro. Layout: Row, binary, schema embedded. Use it for: Streaming and schema evolution (Kafka, Kinesis). Apache Parquet. Layout: Columnar, binary. Use it for: Analytics: Athena, Redshift Spectrum, E M R, Glue; best default for the lake. Apache O R C (Optimized Row Columnar). Layout: Columnar, binary. Use it for: Hive-oriented analytics; often smaller files; richer complex types. Columnar formats compress by column, support predicate pushdown (skip blocks using min or max statistics) and are splittable, so queries read only the needed columns and scan less data.

1.title: File Formats and Conversion, continued
1.text: File Formats and Conversion, continued. Compression: gzip (good ratio, not splittable for text), bzip two (splittable, slow), Snappy and Zstandard (fast; common inside Parquet), L Z O. Convert with Glue jobs (ApplyMapping, write as Parquet), Athena C T A S (create table as select) (format equals 'P A R Q U E T'), Firehose format conversion or E M R or Spark. Avoid tiny files: thousands of small objects slow listing and reads; compact them into files of roughly one hundred twenty-eight megabytes to one gigabyte. Partition the output (for example year equals two thousand twenty-six or month equals eleven or ) so queries can prune partitions. Exam tip: "Reduce Athena cost and speed up queries on C S V data in S three" to convert to Parquet (or O R C), compress, and partition.

1.title: Connecting to and Integrating Data Sources
1.text: Connecting to and Integrating Data Sources. J D B C (Java Database Connectivity) and O D B C (Open Database Connectivity) are standard drivers that let tools and code query relational databases. A W S Glue connections store how to reach a data store: the J D B C U R L, credentials (use A W S Secrets Manager, not clear text), and V P C (Virtual Private Cloud), subnet and security groups; a Glue job reaches one subnet for its connections. Network rule: the database's security group must allow the Glue connection's security group (usually a self-referencing rule); for databases outside A W S, route through a N A T (network address translation) gateway (or V P N (virtual private network) or Direct Connect).

1.title: Connecting to and Integrating Data Sources, continued
1.text: Connecting to and Integrating Data Sources, continued. Redshift and Athena also offer J D B C and O D B C drivers for B I (business intelligence) tools; the Amazon Redshift Data A P I is the driverless, H T T P alternative (section seven). Integrating several sources: join and union in Spark (Glue or E M R), catalog every source with crawlers so S Q L engines see one schema, use federated query (Athena or Redshift) to join without copying, standardize keys, types and time zones, and de-duplicate. Keep raw data unchanged in a landing zone, write cleaned data to a curated zone. Exam tip: A Glue job in a V P C cannot reach the database: check security groups, subnet routing, N A T or V P C endpoints, and that credentials come from Secrets Manager.

1.title: Cost while processing
1.text: Cost while processing. Right-size. Pick the smallest worker type that fits; avoid over-provisioning D P U s; use auto scaling. Flex and Spot. Glue Flex execution; E M R Spot instances for task nodes; Spot for Batch and E C S (Elastic Container Service). Do not run idle. Transient E M R clusters, E M R Serverless, Glue (pay per run), Lambda (pay per invocation). Read less data. Columnar formats, partitioning, push-down filters, only the columns needed. Fewer, bigger files. Compact small files; reduce S three requests and task overhead. Choose the cheaper engine. Lambda for tiny steps; Athena per T B scanned for occasional S Q L; Redshift for steady heavy S Q L.

1.title: Cost while processing, continued
1.text: Cost while processing, continued. Set timeouts and limits. Glue job timeout, maximum capacity, cost controls on E M R Serverless applications; A W S Budgets alerts and A W S Cost Explorer to see which jobs cost the most.

1.title: Containers (Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS)
1.text: Containers (Amazon E C S, Amazon E K S). Run custom or long-running transforms in containers: Amazon E C S (A W S-native orchestrator) or Amazon E K S (Kubernetes); store images in Amazon E C R (Elastic Container Registry). Launch types: A W S Fargate (serverless, you set C P U and memory per task) or E C two (you manage the instances, cheaper at steady high use). Optimize for performance: set task C P U and memory to the real need, use auto scaling on queue depth or C P U, use Spot capacity for fault-tolerant batch, keep images small, and place tasks close to the data.

1.title: Containers (Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS), continued
1.text: Containers (Amazon E C S, Amazon E K S), continued. A W S Batch runs batch jobs on containers with a queue and compute environment (E C two, Spot or Fargate): a fit for many independent jobs. Exam tip: "Long-running or custom-runtime transformation that does not fit Lambda or Glue" to a container on E C S or E K S (Fargate for no servers). "Thousands of batch jobs" to A W S Batch.

1.title: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs
1.text: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs. Out of memory (driver or executor). Likely cause: Collecting too much to the driver, big partitions, too small a worker. Fix: Larger or memory-optimized worker (G two X, R types), more partitions, avoid collecting. One slow task. Likely cause: Data skew: a few keys hold most rows. Fix: Salt hot keys, enable adaptive query execution, repartition. Slow reads, many requests. Likely cause: Many small files. Fix: Group files, compact upstream, use columnar formats. Slow joins and shuffles. Likely cause: Wide shuffles of large tables. Fix: Broadcast the small table, filter early, partition on the join key.

2.title: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs, continued
2.text: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs, continued. Cannot connect. Likely cause: Security group, route, N A T, credentials, S S L (Secure Sockets Layer). Fix: Check the connection's V P C settings, security groups, Secrets Manager secret. Access denied. Likely cause: I A M (Identity and Access Management) role of the job or Lake Formation permissions. Fix: Fix the job role and S three or Lake Formation grants. Job reprocesses old data. Likely cause: Bookmark off, or source path changed. Fix: Enable bookmarks, keep transformation ctx stable. Lambda times out. Likely cause: fifteen-minute limit, too little memory. Fix: Split work, raise memory, or use Glue or Step Functions. Throttling. Likely cause: A P I or service limits. Fix: Backoff, more capacity, batching (Module one).

2.title: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs, continued
2.text: Troubleshooting Failures and Slow Jobs, continued. Tools: CloudWatch metrics and logs (continuous logging), Glue job metrics and observability metrics, Spark U I with event logs in S three, Glue job run insights, E M R step and container logs, Athena query statistics. Exam tip: "A Spark job fails with OutOfMemoryError" to a bigger or memory-optimized worker and fewer large partitions. "One task takes hours, others seconds" to data skew.

2.title: Data APIs: Making Data Available to Other Systems
2.text: Data A P I s: Making Data Available to Other Systems. Amazon A P I Gateway exposes R E S T (representational state transfer), H T T P and WebSocket A P I s in front of Lambda, DynamoDB, Athena queries or other backends; it handles authentication (I A M, Cognito, Lambda authorizers), throttling and usage plans, caching and monitoring. Amazon Redshift Data A P I: run S Q L over H T T P S with the S D K (software development kit), no drivers, no persistent connections, no network setup; calls are asynchronous; authenticate with Secrets Manager, temporary I A M credentials or I A M Identity Center; a query can run up to twenty-four hours and results are kept twenty-four hours (five hundred megabytes maximum result). Athena has its own A P I (StartQueryExecution, GetQueryResults) for programs.

2.title: Data APIs: Making Data Available to Other Systems, continued
2.text: Data A P I s: Making Data Available to Other Systems, continued. A W S Lambda function U R L s give a function an H T T P S endpoint. Design points: paginate, cache hot results, limit result sizes, secure with I A M or tokens, and throttle to protect the backend. Edge and network: Amazon Route fifty-three gives the A P I a friendly D N S name, Amazon CloudFront can cache responses close to users, and A W S W A F (Web Application Firewall) (web exploits and bots) and A W S Shield (DDoS) protect a public A P I. Exam tip: "A Lambda function must run S Q L on Redshift without managing connections or drivers" to Redshift Data A P I.

2.title: Volume, Velocity and Variety
2.text: Volume, Velocity and Variety. The figure shows this: The three Vs of data: volume (how much), velocity (how fast) and variety (structured, semi-structured and unstructured).

2.title: Volume, Velocity and Variety, continued
2.text: Volume, Velocity and Variety, continued. Volume. Question it answers: How much data? Effect on design: Distributed processing (Spark), S three storage, partitioning, compression. Velocity. Question it answers: How fast does it arrive and how fast must it be used? Effect on design: Streaming services (Kinesis, M S K (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka), Flink) versus batch. Variety. Question it answers: How many shapes and sources? Effect on design: Schema-on-read, catalogs, formats, specialized stores. Structured: rows and columns with a fixed schema (relational tables, C S V with a header): R D S (Relational Database Service), Aurora, Redshift. Semi-structured: self-describing (Jason, X M L, Avro, logs): DynamoDB, DocumentDB, S three with Athena, OpenSearch. Unstructured: no schema (images, audio, video, P D F s, free text): S three, then processing with A I (artificial intelligence) services or L L M s (large language model).

2.title: Using Large Language Models in Data Processing
2.text: Using Large Language Models in Data Processing. Amazon Bedrock gives A P I access to foundation models; a pipeline calls it from Lambda, Glue, Step Functions or a container (InvokeModel or Converse). Typical data-engineering uses: classify or tag text (the delivery notes), extract fields from documents, summarize records, clean or standardize free text, and create embeddings for vector search. Batch inference: submit many prompts at once (input files in S three), responses are written to S three asynchronously: the right choice for large, non-interactive datasets; on-demand calls suit interactive or small workloads. Knowledge bases for Amazon Bedrock turn your documents into vector embeddings for retrieval-augmented generation (R A G) (Module nine).

2.title: Using Large Language Models in Data Processing, continued
2.text: Using Large Language Models in Data Processing, continued. Amazon Kendra is intelligent enterprise search over documents; Amazon Q is a generative A I assistant that can help build and explain data integration code. Cost and safety: L L M calls cost per token, so filter first, cache repeated results and batch; keep personal data out of prompts or protect it with Bedrock Guardrails. Out of scope for this exam: training or tuning M L (machine learning) models and M L inference design. Exam tip: "Classify millions of text records overnight at the lowest cost" to Bedrock batch inference with S three input and output.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Glue: Serverless Spark E T L; D P U equals four virtual C P Us, sixteen gigabytes. E M R: Managed Hadoop or Spark or Hive or Presto; E C two, E K S or Serverless; primary or core or task (Spot) nodes; transient clusters. Lambda: Small event-driven transforms; fifteen-minute limit. S Q L E T L: Athena C T A S or insert into on S three; Redshift in-warehouse E L T (extract, load, transform). DataBrew: Visual no-code preparation. Formats: Parquet or O R C columnar (analytics), Avro (streams, schema), C S V or Jason (exchange); compress, partition, compact small files. Connections: J D B C or O D B C; Glue connection equals U R L plus Secrets Manager plus V P C or subnet or security groups; N A T for outside A W S. Containers: E C S or E K S on Fargate or E C two; Batch for many jobs; right-size C P U and memory. Troubleshoot: O O M (out of memory) to bigger worker; skew to salt or A Q E (adaptive query execution); small files to group; connect to V P C, S G, secret.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Kestrel Freight needs serverless E T L that cleans nightly C S V files, uses the A W S Glue Data Catalog, and requires as little infrastructure management as possible. Which service fits best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. A W S Glue is serverless Spark E T L integrated with the Data Catalog. E M R on E C two and E C two fleets require cluster or instance management.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. A team queries large C S V files in S three with Amazon Athena and the cost and runtime are too high. What should the engineer do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. Columnar, compressed and partitioned data lets Athena read only the needed columns and partitions, so it scans less data. Jason is larger and slower to query.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. An Apache Spark job on A W S Glue fails with OutOfMemoryError during a large aggregation. Which two actions are most likely to help? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. More memory per worker and smaller partitions reduce memory pressure. Collecting everything to the driver makes it worse.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. A transformation job finishes quickly for most keys but one task runs for hours because a single key holds most of the rows. What is this problem and a fix? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C. One key holding most rows is data skew; salting the key or enabling adaptive query execution spreads the work.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. A Lambda function must run S Q L statements on Amazon Redshift without managing database drivers, persistent connections, or V P C networking from the function. Which option should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D. The Data A P I provides an H T T P S endpoint, uses Secrets Manager or temporary credentials, and needs no drivers or persistent connections.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A company must classify several million free-text delivery notes once a night at the lowest cost, and no one waits for the results. Which approach is best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A. Batch inference processes many prompts asynchronously from S three and writes results to S three, which suits large non-interactive jobs. Training a model is out of scope and unnecessary.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which statement about columnar file formats is correct? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Columnar formats such as Parquet and O R C compress by column and support predicate pushdown and column pruning, which reduces the data scanned.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. A Glue job in a V P C must read from a PostgreSQL database. The job fails to connect. Which action should the engineer take first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B. Connection failures are usually network or credential issues: verify the connection's V P C settings, the security-group rules between the job and the database, and the secret.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all eight answers. Question one: D. Question two: C. Question three: A and C. Question four: C. Question five: D. Question six: A. Question seven: B. Question eight: B. In the next module, we continue the course.
